tasks.short: Notify dispatch or mechanics of vehicle problems

steps.what: Notify dispatchers or company mechanics of vehicle problems and clarify symptoms

tasks.design: Retain direct reporting through {TELEPHONY}, including urgent contact and symptom clarification. No separate report-writing workload or automated roadworthiness decision is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Vehicle problems are situational and may require immediate clarification.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software step establishes a saving in the direct notification itself.
tasks.still_hard: The driver must describe symptoms accurately and follow the relevant stop or assistance procedure.
tasks.human_edge: The driver observes the actual vehicle and makes clear when immediate help is needed.
tasks.altitude: Direct problem reporting and escalation remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify symptoms and advise the permitted next action
reach.learn: Describe warning signs without claiming a diagnosis

evidence.claim: Direct vehicle-fault notification needs symptom clarification; no measured automation saving is established for this task.

assumptions: Boundary is notifying and clarifying the problem, not inspection, repair, dispatch decisions or a separate defect report.

The driver produces vehicle identity, location and symptom description through observation and the conversation in s1. All capture and reporting time remains; there is no ready fault code or urgency flag.
Existing phone and reporting procedures remain unchanged. No new integration or machine triage is proposed, so new upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Is any duplicate written report required outside this direct notification task?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; direct notification is unchanged. Gross and net zero with no new upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Give passengers local information or advice

steps.what: Provide passengers with local information or advice about places, hotels or restaurants

tasks.design: Keep the passenger conversation with the driver, supported by any existing visitor reference in {DOCS}. No new lookup or generated recommendation is introduced into the driving task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice depends on what the passenger wants and what the driver knows reliably.
tasks.enabler_now: No digital change establishes a saving in this mainly conversational task.
tasks.still_hard: Opening hours, suitability and passenger preferences may be uncertain.
tasks.human_edge: The driver asks a useful question, gives practical context and states uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Passenger assistance remains a direct service responsibility.

reach.task: Maintain checked general visitor information for drivers
reach.learn: Distinguish stable location information from current availability

evidence.claim: Local passenger advice remains a human conversation in this task-specific assessment.

assumptions: Boundary is the driver's direct information and advice, not booking services, paid recommendations or destination routing.
Preferences are obtained in s1 with all time retained. No structured passenger profile or live opening-hours feed is assumed.
Existing references remain unchanged; no new reference-maintenance duty is assigned to another role. Any existing adjacent reference work earns no saving here.
No new system or work process is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Questions commonly asked and available references
research_questions: Are repeated factual lookups a measurable part of the task, when the vehicle is safely stopped?

already_counted.description: Passenger question, explanation and uncertainty handling

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; no conversational work is removed. Gross and net zero with zero upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report to the garage and receive vehicle assignments

steps.what: Report to taxicab services and receive the dispatcher-approved vehicle assignment
Attend the garage, clarify assignment problems and receive the assigned vehicle

tasks.design: Show the existing dispatcher-approved assignment in a native driver view in {OPS_SYSTEM}, retaining {TELEPHONY} for questions. The driver checks it at a safe stopping point and still attends the garage, receives the vehicle and resolves mismatches.
tasks.previous_blocker: An already selected vehicle assignment is repeatedly relayed verbally or by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: A native read-only driver view can show the same approved assignment without a new allocation algorithm.
tasks.still_hard: Vehicle changes, key handover and assignment mismatches need people on site.
tasks.human_edge: The driver notices a mismatch between the displayed assignment and the actual handover.
tasks.altitude: Receive clearer assignment details while retaining normal garage and vehicle checks.

reach.learn: Assignment versions and who may change an allocation

evidence.claim: A native view of an existing dispatcher-approved assignment may reduce repeated relay time; this is an E1 scenario, not a cited taxi case.

assumptions: Boundary is reporting for and receiving the assignment. Vehicle allocation, driving, detailed pre-trip inspection and dispatcher labour are unchanged and earn no saving.

The dispatcher already produces driver or shift ID, vehicle ID, garage, start time, assignment version and approved status in the existing dispatch process. The design reuses this record and requires no extra dispatcher capture. If there is no existing record, stay with verbal assignment rather than assume free creation.

In s1 the driver checks identity, vehicle, time, location and version within 21 remaining hours; missing or conflicting details go to s2. No automated roadworthiness or driver eligibility flag is required.

All physical attendance and handover remain in s2. Native view configuration is tested before code; existing views or useful conversations do not yield a new saving. Any employee consultation required for access or monitoring is included in rollout.
unknowns: Existence of a complete dispatcher-owned assignment record
Current repeated relay time and native driver view
research_questions: Can the driver read the exact current approved assignment without extra dispatcher entry?

already_counted.description: Assignment reading, identity checks and queries
Garage attendance, handover and mismatch resolution

incremental.description: Check assignment-view access and field settings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=21+65=86; gross 14%, less 2 upkeep gives net 12%. Low 0 if no existing structured assignment or if a native view already serves the driver. Physical handover is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Start and stop the taximeter at trip boundaries

steps.what: Turn taximeter on when passengers enter the cab
Turn taximeter off when passengers reach the final destination

tasks.design: Keep start and stop actions with the driver using the existing {OTHER} taximeter. The meter's existing fare arithmetic is runtime already provided by equipment and earns no new human saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Boarding and final arrival are real-world events requiring the correct trip boundary.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software-only change establishes a reliable boundary event without extra capture or changed meter controls.
tasks.still_hard: Intermediate stops, changed destinations and unusual boarding circumstances can make a location signal insufficient.
tasks.human_edge: The driver confirms the actual passenger trip boundaries.
tasks.altitude: Meter operation and fare accountability remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify meter procedures for exceptional trip boundaries

evidence.claim: Existing meter calculations are not a new saving in driver start and stop actions; the assessment is E1.

assumptions: Boundary is starting and stopping the meter, not driving, tariff-setting, payment or trip reporting.
The driver observes boarding in s1 and confirms final arrival in s2, retaining all time. No free structured occupied-seat, final-arrival or destination-change signal is assumed.
The native taximeter and its approved controls remain unchanged; no geofence, sensor or booking-app connection is introduced.
No new process or equipment maintenance is created, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Meter type and local operating requirements
research_questions: Which exceptional trip boundaries require driver confirmation under the local meter procedure?

already_counted.description: Final arrival confirmation and meter stop

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=50+50=100; start and stop actions remain. Gross and net zero, with no new upkeep. Existing fare calculation is not counted as labour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated assignment relay where existing records support it while retaining passenger service, meter control and fault escalation.
role.ambitious_version: A driver with clear assignment information and protected attention for passengers and the vehicle.
